summary.text: Greg Steube is the Republican U.S. Representative for Florida's 17th District, in office since January 2019, and won re-election on November 3, 2026, according to unofficial results.
An attorney and Army veteran, he served in the Florida House and Senate before his election to Congress and sits on the Ways and Means and Intelligence committees.
His official biography highlights his military service, work for seniors and agriculture, and conservative immigration positions.

paragraphs.text: Steube was born in Manatee County, Florida, in 1978; Wikipedia gives his birth date as May 19, 1978.
He earned his bachelor's degree in 2000 and his law degree in 2003, both from the University of Florida.
According to his official biography he enlisted in the U.S. Army while in law school, and he served from 2004 to 2008 as an airborne infantry officer and judge advocate general.

The biography says that after an injury in Ranger school he transferred to the Army JAG Corps, serving as Chief of Detainee Operations for Multinational Division North in Iraq with the 25th Infantry Division from 2006 to 2007 and then as a JAG prosecuting courts-martial.
Steube served in the Florida House of Representatives from 2010 to 2016 and in the Florida State Senate from 2016 to 2018.

He won election to the U.S. House in 2018 and took office in January 2019, succeeding Rep. Thomas Rooney; his office describes him as in his fourth term, and he ran for re-election in 2026 after an uncontested Republican primary.

In 2025 and 2026 he serves on the House Committee on Ways and Means, on its Health and Trade subcommittees, and on the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence; he earlier served on the Veterans' Affairs, Oversight, Judiciary and Foreign Affairs committees.
His official biography says he lives in Sarasota with his wife, Jennifer, and their son.
He won the November 3, 2026 general election with 58.5% of the vote to Matthew Montavon's 40.1%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
